body:

However, the interface and over all look is very much aimed at children and young adults. 

I like that you get rewards, helps boost that dopamine, but as an adult, I don’t want the reward to be a new emoji icon or stars falling down when I tick something off the list. 

As I said, great for kids and young adults but it was way too immature for me. 

Have an adult option where the rewards are like a free one on one with a specialist for an amount of points to you’ve accumulated. Something that will really help adults coping with ADHD.

title: Routinen aufbauen für Neurodiverse
body:
Numo ist klasse, um sich seine Gewohnheiten zurechtzuzimmern, neu zu ordnen und abzuarbeiten.
Es gibt Aufgaben und Routinen, die sich im Tag ordnen und über Etikett filtern lassen. Beide ggf mit motivierender Notiz und Unteraufgaben.

Wenn die Liste steht, kannst du jede Aufgabe der Reihe nach angehen. Ein Timer hilft dir, ins Rollen zu kommen, oder auch ein Ende zu finden.

Numo hat Communities eingebaut, mit denen du deine Fortschritte teilen kannst.
Viel Feedback um deine Erfolge zu feiern und dran zu bleiben.

Kleine Abzüge in der B-Note bzgl Stabilität.
Tipp: Routinen bearbeiten unter Home → Pläne → Routinen, nicht unter Bevorstehende, dann wird’s auch gespeichert. 

Nicht für Projektpläne gemacht, aber für Deinen Tag.

title: Une appli géniale, mais un prix vraiment excessif !!!!
body: J’ai testé beaucoup d’applications pour m’aider avec mon TDAH et celle-ci est clairement celle qui m’a le plus aidée. Contrairement à d’autres applications qu’on utilise à outrance les premiers jours car le design et la nouveauté nous donnent un pic de dopamine mais qu’on finit rapidement par abandonner, l’interface et la simplicité de celle-ci nous fait rester bien plus facilement ! D’autant plus que les mises à jour sont fréquentes. Un gros défaut est que l’application ne nous présente pas pas-à-pas ses fonctionnalités quand nous nous y connectons pour la première fois. Lors de la première connexion, nous sommes vraiment perdus, et je ne vais pas mentir, je me suis dit que l’application avait l’air nulle au départ !! Voici comment se présente l’application : - un onglet « to-do-list », on l’on peut cocher toutes les tâches déjà faites et organiser celles à faire (avec un historique de toutes les tâches faites dans le passé ce qui est très gratifiant !!) - un onglet « squad », où vous pouvez voir l’activité d’autres utilisateurs de votre « team » et où vous pouvez poster des messages, ce qui permet de se sentir accompagné (vos tâches publiques apparaissent automatiquement dans l’activité, ce qui est très motivant car tout le monde voit ce que vous faites au cours de la journée) - un onglet « stories », avec des astuces basées sur la thérapie comportementale, qui ont l’air parfois simplistes mais qui m’ont beaucoup aidées en complément de la Ritaline !! - un onglet social, où vous pouvez faire des posts et voir ceux de tous les autres utilisateurs de l’application, où vous pouvez partager des tips, des anecdotes, etc Pour autant, son prix est vraiment excessif, et comme la plupart de ses utilisateurs, je suis dans l’incompréhension. Comparé à des applications comme Tiimo qui selon les personnes peuvent être des aides précieuses mais qui restent accessibles avec des tarifs au mois mais aussi à l’année très avantageux, le tarif pour un seul mois (17,99€) est presque aussi cher que certaines applications à l’année ! Il n’existe en plus que deux abonnements : au mois, et pour 6 mois (69,99€ ????? donc au final 120€ pour un an ????). Cela me met vraiment en colère, car pour une application qui se veut inclusive, ceci est un tarif que peu de personnes peuvent se permettre d’accepter. L’application gagnerait d’autant plus en utilisateurs si elle était moins chère (cela permettrait d’avoir beaucoup plus d’utilisateurs de nos pays respectifs plutôt que de devoir forcément communiquer en anglais avec les membres de notre squad). Pourquoi ne pas lancer un tarif libre, pour que les personnes TDAH avec peu de revenus puissent bénéficier de l’application au même titre que les autres ? Je serais prête à payer plus cher si cela permettait à d’autres d’utiliser l’application à un moindre prix voire même gratuitement, mais pour l’application actuelle, le prix est vraiment excessif. Par ailleurs, l’application comporte de nombreux bugs, ce qui est difficilement compréhensible quand on voit le prix de l’application (raison pour laquelle j’enlève une étoile ; pour un tarif pareil, j’attends une application impeccable). J’ajouterai également que cela rajoute de la culpabilité aux personnes TDAH, qui sont honteuses de devoir payer un prix aussi cher pour une to-do-list (c’est un argument que j’ai plusieurs fois vus dans les posts de la communauté de personnes annonçant arrêter leur abonnement). Cependant, si vous en avez les moyens, je recommande quand même cette application aux personnes dont le TDAH est très handicapant dans leurs vies. Car étrangement, malgré le principe vraiment simpliste de l’application, ça fonctionne là où ça ne fonctionnerait pas si nous le faisions nous-mêmes ! Mais si vous n’en avez pas les moyens, ne faites pas l’essai gratuit, car cela serait très frustrant pour vous dans le futur d’avoir testé une application qui vous aurait aidé sans avoir la possibilité de continuer à l’utiliser. J’ai d’ailleurs moi-même hésité à reprendre l’abonnement à cause du prix après l’avoir suspendu pendant des vacances, car j’hésitais grandement à remettre ce prix tout en ayant le doute que tous les TDAH ont, à savoir, vais-je vraiment l’utiliser à nouveau ? En conclusion : une appli vraiment super et qui m’a énormément aidée, mais s’il vous plaît, baissez le prix 🙏🏻🙏🏻🙏🏻🙏🏻

title: Day 518 and still the best, simplest tool for ADHD support
body:
Need I say more? I love this app. I’ve tried many, and this is the only one that’s stayed the course. We all have our preferences, different mashups of neurodivergent traits, usually with a few other bits and bobs thrown in to keep it spicy. But Numo is by far the best one for my individual characteristics and personality. I enjoy the little dopamine shots when I see my daily streak, earn new colours, sounds, etc. 
The best part is ticking my to-do list. I don’t always tick everything, but it lets me see what I’ve done and haven’t done. I’ve learnt I do more than I think - or remember - I have and that’s a little boost in itself. I can remind myself if things i need to do in the near or distant future and I don’t have to think about it. Much better than my phone calendar which I often miss (it’s too dreary, boring, and makes me feel anxious) and alarms often don’t play! Numo is a nice place to wake up to and see what’s in store - everything from brushing my teeth (right ADHDers?) to friends birthdays and paying bills. Daily, weekly, monthly, one-off or pretty much any combination. 
Finally, any problems with it have been quickly dealt with by the Numo team.
I fully expect ti write a similar one in another 518 days - especially if I add a task in Numo!! Thank you for creating it ☺️🙏⚡️❤️

title: 5 stars, but the social side still needs work
body:
I honestly didn’t see myself using this app for any real length of time, but it’s turned out to be my favourite place to manage those random to-do items I’m constantly forgetting - like what day the bins go out, or that I need to teach myself how to remove a hard drive so I can bin an old desktop. 

I like that reminders can be entered as one-offs or repeating habits. I like the option to share tasks I complete publicly, or not. 

I would love it if they had a way you could combine multiple tasks into an overall task, with the original tasks as subtasks - sometimes I don’t realise tasks are linked until I’m several in, and copying those manually is bleh.

I don’t fully understand the social stuff, but I appreciate that the developers are trying new things out. Just give us a forum style place where we can raise topics and ask (and search) for questions and answers people have shared. Keep the global social feed (the ability to like and reply), but give us a “friends” feed and let us connect with people we want to see in it.

Also, as great as this app is I really struggle to see myself paying the £9.99 a month subscription. £4.99? Hell yes. But this shouldn’t cost more than paramount+. 

Those are the most constructive thoughts I could share, but this really is a useful and weirdly, wonderfully rewarding way to keep me in touch with my daily and random to-do’s!

title: Irritating and counterproductive
body:

I’m working on my Macbook mid-morning when my iPhone lights up. “Hey! Got a few minutes for a procrastination story!?”

No! NO!! I have not. I’m doing my work!!! 

You’re supposed to HELP me focus. Not distract me yourself!!!!

You … you … yes. I’m going to say it. Unlike any ADHDer, Numo App:

YOU HAD ONE JOB!!!!!!!!!

As for that cartoon nonsense …

“Cringe-free”? More like cringe-ful. 

This app purports to be for all ages but looks more aimed at 14yos than 40yos. Maybe I’m not the target market. 

I don’t want a “non-serious” username like, say, HyperfocusHound or ADDicted2Luv. ADHD can be a superpower as well as a curse but I’ve had quite enough of it being a hideous curse. 

Staying focused at work so I don’t get fired isn’t funny or cute. It’s life or death. The grinning strawberry doesn’t make me feel better. Instead, it lowers my opinion of the developers so rapidly there’s a sonic boom.

title: Fake Reviews & High Subscription Fees
body:
On the surface this is a great idea and could be an amazing app. The premise of it is simple, easy to set up and fun, however, I agree with a lot of the genuine reviews on here that the execution is pretty basic and lacking a lot of functionality. 

The UI is nice and clean but the UX is poor and as a person with ADHD I find it mildly frustrating to use at times which is the opposite of what you want.

eg. You can't reorder your todo list or set priorities so everything is out of order, meaning you have to search your to do list for what you have to do or before you type it out in the morning you've got to plan your day out completely then type in order = Not so great for people with ADHD.

The tools are a nice touch but after you complete things like the emotion map, they disappear off into the ether to be immediately forgotten about...and the tone of voice used in the app can be pretty condescending at times.

This app has a long loooooong way to go but given they charge over £15/month, it's not worth the pain and the developer response essentially saying 'ADHD coaching is $200 so we're doing you a favour' is pretty shocking.

There are far more developed apps designed for ADHD that also aren't perfect but cost around £25/year and clearly put a lot more focus into the user experience.

Test your app better.

title: App is mediocre but has big potential
body:
The concept of the app seems very appealing but it just hasn’t been executed very well. The list function is okay but you can’t reorder tasks to prioritise what you need to get done first (incase you burn out midway through getting things done). It also glitches sometimes when you try to add the task to your task page. It’s like a glorified version of the Apple List app but with less flexibility. The ‘hacks’ are kind of patronising, example: “If it takes less than 5 minutes to do the task, just do it immediately”???? 

I do however like the ‘Squad’ page where people can interact with your tasks. Only problem is that you don’t get a notification or a page that collates your reactions to keep you motivated. It just comes up on the squad page if you catch it at the right time alongside with everyone else’s random tasks. 

The ‘Learn’ page is nice but I never really get around to using it. I have to end one course to be able to start a new one which means I don’t get to read the new topic I’ve become interested in and I don’t look at the current topic because it temporarily does not interest me. I cannot commit to going through a whole story and doing all of their inbuilt tasks in one go.

If it had a similar layout to Instagram I think it would actually work really well.  A ‘Learn’ page being similar to the Explore page to pick up quick tips and tricks, a notification centre showing you all the people congratulating you on finishing tasks (for a lil dopamine hit) and your home page showing everyone else doing their tasks.

I do understand that this app is in its early stages of development and I have high hopes for the future but I will probably go back to writing lists in my notepad.

title: Great tool, makes life less overwhelming
body:
I’ve been using the app for about 10 days. It has made tasks & life in general less overwhelming. Obviously, there are similar apps out there, so here are specific things I like about this one:
(sorry for any misspelling 😁) 

1)  COMMUNITY:  I have a hard time on social media apps. I feel like I join them to keep in touch with friends, but I rarely see posts from my own friends on my feed. Instead, I get drowned in random content from accounts I don’t know, which can be nice… but it doesn’t make me feel engaged with MY community. They overwhelm me & give me anxiety. 
But…
Numo allows me to connect with people and give and receive support. You join a team of your own choosing, engage with them as much as you have the capacity, AND there are no random content or interactions from accounts that you never asked for. You don’t end up losing 3 hours of your day on content you never intended to consume.
💕Best part is that I know literally everyone on the app has ADHD & I learn so much about my own brain from others!!! 💕

2)  TASKS: 
         a)  You can choose to make tasks a 1-time thing or a routine. For routines, you can schedule it on specific days & times. 
          b) When creating tasks, you can break them into sub-tasks. And you can complete a general task even if you skipped a sub-task. 

3) 💕STREAKS:  I like that the streak is for the number of days you engage with the app. So, even if you skip a routine, as long as you complete 1 task that day & engage with your team, you don’t lose your streak. 
For me losing a streak is a HUGE discouraging thing. I might just give up on using the app. So, it’s nice that there’s no pressure on completing EVERYTHING just so I don’t lose my streak.

The app design is top-tier for (my) ADHD. The interface is minimalistic, colorful, and simple to use. It has satisfying sounds and haptics, but not so much as to be annoying. It has a reward system for using the app and its features. The rewards only unlock aesthetics (themes, icons, etc.). It has a community feature which I have yet to use. 

Cons: 

The app has some minor typos. It has learning courses that are concise. It has a reader function for the text and some memes to go along with it. The app allows you to customize the speed of the reader and also the time delay after the slide is finished. HOWEVER, my experience with the customization was disappointing. I don’t like to hear a voice while reading text. I’d rather just read the text without the voice; or, listen to the voice while associated images are displayed. The problem I’ve noticed: I can turn off the voice but the slides automatically move on and I can’t read fast enough or process the information before it advances. This, of course, depends on your reading speed. For me, this is a MAJOR block to using the app effectively, and I would love to have an option to advance slides MANUALLY. 

Overall, I’d gladly give it 5 stars and will update my review if this ever gets changed. The app is wonderful to look at and use! Thank you for inviting me to the clinical trial, I’m looking forward to improving my ADHD symptoms using it.

title: Solid proof of concept, priced as if highly polished
body:
This app is on to something amazing, and I wish I could stay subscribed. I love the social media story-style lessons, the community aspect is excellent, and the way the to-do list can break down and prioritize is so helpful!

However, there is a lack of polish that makes it hard to justify the current cost ($59.99 for only six months). Here are the things I noticed that are keeping me from subscribing.

1) Repeating tasks. The limited options work out fine for me, but these tasks will disappear from your list if left incomplete (except for daily). While a regular task will show that it’s overdue, repeating tasks won't. If I have a weekly or monthly task, I need it to stay until I complete it, not limit it to just that one day.

2) Tools introduced in lessons aren't always accessible. Specifically, I love the “find an absurdly small first step to touch your task” hack, but a way to trigger that guidance with any task would be so helpful! I'm sure that's not the only one.

3) Reliance on AI. To be clear, I love the AI features! Super helpful when you cannot make decisions yourself. However, if I want to do the manual prioritization, I must wait for the AI to load first. Sometimes it won't load, so I can't access the manual option that I often prefer. Similarly, I cannot manually add task breakdowns after the AI split. It's either accept or deny the suggested splits only.

I enjoyed my 5 weeks using this app, but I can't justify the cost given the polish it needs to be worth it. I'm sad that I won't have Numo to use day by day, but I know that it's too much of a financial commitment for me. Numo, I hope you consider some of these changes and polishes that your app deserves because this will help so many ADHDers.

title: Tried so many apps - this one is by far the best
body:
I have ADHD and struggle constantly with task management. I’ve tried lots of methods and apps, and nothing has really worked for me so far. A lot of the apps, even if they were fun at first, got to be a task in and of themselves, and the rewards for using the app were low. Most of them are basically glorified to-do lists.

This app is stimulating to look at, uses game-like wording and structure, has lots of mini-courses to help manage different parts of your life (with audio, text, and images that play through automatically - I didn’t zone out at all, which is saying something), forces you to set rewards for yourself for certain tasks, and uses peer support, which is super helpful.

While some of the information isn’t particularly new to me (I’ve read a lot about procrastination, for example), it’s phrased in this straightforward, no-nonsense way that still acknowledges the difficulty of some of these tasks, and it’s addressed specifically to ADHD problems, rather than just general organization issues. It’s incredibly refreshing.

Overall, it really feels like this app was designed specifically for people with ADHD, as opposed to other apps, which feel like basic productivity helpers marketed toward ADHD-ers to take advantage of the demographic. If you have ADHD, really can’t recommend it enough.

title: It’s a cool idea but needs work. Right now it is not worth the price tag.
body:
This is a pretty cool app which allows you to read other peoples tips and tricks for dealing with their ADHD as well as post things you might need help with and get feedback. The problem is that it’s very hard to find your post after you’ve published it and there doesn’t seem to be a way to easily view peoples comments on it without endlessly scrolling to find your post again. 

The to do list feature, prioritization, and prompts to break down your task into the smallest bits to help you get started were all super helpful for me, but I can easily do all of that myself with a pen and paper for free. 

The stories they provide contain information on motivation, procrastination, emotional regulation, etc.. They break concepts down into easily understandable bits. 
However, I personally knew all of the tactics provided just from reading, watching ADHD Youtubers, and viewing content on other platforms. 
It’s great to have these resources in one place, I cannot deny that. But I don’t think it is enough to justify a $16 a month subscription.

You can see other peoples posts and respond to them but there is no way to message anyone directly (which I understand) or to add someone as a friend (which I don’t understand).
Your “squad” is assigned to you (unless you invite your IRL friends and they download the app to join you). There’s no messaging feature in the “squad” either or a way to encourage others besides just liking their posts and to do lists. It doesn’t feel like there is a real way to build community and support networks on this app, which was part of the marketing and what I was looking for.   

I think the concept of this app is awesome. And I would gladly come back to it in the future if it had more to offer. 

The team behind the app is easy to contact and they respond rather quickly. 

I have a lot of hope for the future of Numo! And I can’t wait to check back later to see what was added, but right now it’s just not worth the cost for me.

title: ADHD behind a huge paywall
body: Look, I absolutely agree that developers should be paid for their hard work. However, to take advantage of people with ADHD (which is a federally recognized disability) by putting resources to help manage it behind a paywall to the tune of $16/month when most of America is struggling financially is absurd. Especially when there are SO many reported bugs! In a previous response to the price from the developers on another review, they mentioned having a 4 person team they needed to pay to work full time on the app. There shouldn’t be this many bugs from a full time team. It seems the switch to full time development was too eager too soon. I just can’t justify the cost.
